fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear overhead and side clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Mark any gates within fenced sections with reflective numbers or labels so responders can quickly identify which gate leads to which area of the property.
• Keep all gates in fenced sections unlocked or secured with a single standard padlock to allow responders to move between sections without delay.
• Clear a path through any dense vegetation that blocks movement between the front and rear of the property.
• Identify and mark the most direct route from the front driveway to the rear of the property for responders who arrive at the front.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles along the edges so fire apparatus can stage or turn around without obstruction.
• Trim shrubs and low-hanging branches along walkways so responders carrying equipment can move without obstruction.
• If rear access is blocked by a fence or vegetation, install a clearly marked gate to allow responders to reach the back of the property without returning to the front.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging any part of the house.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing immediately alongside the house and any attached structures.
• Keep grass around the structure mowed short, especially during dry periods.
• Maintain clear overhead clearance along all driveway routes by trimming low-hanging branches.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so vegetation does not form a continuous path toward the structure.
• Remove dead or dry grass buildup along the base of any fences or walls connected to the house.
